week.note: Secondary analysis: developer-weeks are repeated measures of the same 60 developers, so they are not independent and these p-values are optimistic. Use the developer level for inference.

keyFindings.text: All results come from SIMULATED data generated from stated assumptions (60 developers, 16 weeks). They are not findings about real developers.

Forecasting: the deployed model (gru_raw, chosen on validation) beats the naive last value on both targets (findings per week p = 0.000125, fix rate p = 0.0189); beats the linear trend on both targets (findings per week p = 6.99e-07, fix rate p = 0.00339); ties the 4-week mean on both targets (findings per week p = 0.393, fix rate p = 0.918).

The residual variant (lstm_residual, added post-hoc after the first test results) against the naive last value: beats on findings per week (p = 0.00031); ties on fix rate (p = 0.0625); beats the linear trend on both targets (findings per week p = 1.18e-06, fix rate p = 0.00603); ties the 4-week mean on both targets (findings per week p = 0.848, fix rate p = 0.68).

Risk classification (repeated grouped CV over all developers): XGBoost beats logistic regression (macro-F1 difference +0.052, 95% CI [+0.007, +0.098]); ties persistence (last 4 weeks' score) (macro-F1 difference +0.013, 95% CI [-0.052, +0.074]); beats fix-rate rule (macro-F1 difference +0.197, 95% CI [+0.127, +0.257]); beats majority class (macro-F1 difference +0.304, 95% CI [+0.233, +0.370]).

Recent behaviour is the strongest predictor: no model reliably beats a baseline that simply repeats the last 4 weeks (the 4-week mean for forecasting, persistence for risk), and the classifier's most important feature is past_score_last4.
Round 1 (12 held-out developers, already seen): persistence macro F1 0.55 vs XGBoost 0.37 with the original features. The extended features were added post-hoc.

At developer level, 10 of 21 pairs remain significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (Pearson). Strongest: Severity-weighted load ~ Findings per week (r = +1.00), Fix rate ~ Ignore rate (r = -0.80), Fix rate ~ Repeat rate (r = -0.49), Ignore rate ~ Repeat rate (r = +0.48). Some pairs are related by construction: fix and ignore rates are shares of the same findings, and severity-weighted load is a weighted count of findings.
